hints.title: Key Insight and Observation
hints.text: Because two peaks cannot be adjacent, selecting index i as a peak skips index i - 1.

hints.title: Algorithmic Strategy and State
hints.text: Formulate a state table: dp[p][i] represents the minimum cost to form p peaks within the first i elements.

hints.title: Optimal Boundary and Processing
hints.text: Compute transitions by either skipping index i or paying the cost to make index i a peak combined with dp[p - 1][i - 2].

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Fills a 2D table of size k by n evaluating skip or pick decisions.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Evaluating all combinations of non-adjacent peak indices is exponential.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Stores table of size (k + 1) by n.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Models non-adjacent peak selection using dynamic programming transitions.
